description: AI Agents (inside one system): Use whenever the person asks to change records in a system whose AI agent may change them: every change goes through here first, and nothing is written. Pick one action and give one item per record, at most 25. set_fields: fills, corrects, empties or makes records with the fields describe_record_type lists (type, and id unless it makes a new record; set holds field keys and new values, clear the keys to empty). update_fields: New values for fields of a record that exist in the person's own system, such as a lead status or a custom field, by their own names. (type, id, fields). move_stage: A record moved to another stage or status of its pipeline, such as a deal to proposal sent or to won; a won or lost stage closes the record. (type, id, stage; optional pipeline). add_note: A note on a record's timeline in the person's system. (type, id, text; optional at, user). add_task: A task or follow up on a record in the person's system, such as a call next week; the system may notify the user it is assigned to. (type, id, subject, due_at; optional notes, priority, task_kind, done, user). update_task: A task or follow up that already exists moved to another date, retitled, reassigned or marked done, by the id list_related_records or search_tasks gives it; only what is given changes. (task_id; optional type, id, subject, due_at, notes, done, user). log_activity: A call or meeting that took place, written on a record's timeline in the person's system; nothing is dialled and no invitation is sent. (type, id, kind, title; optional notes, at, end_at, user). add_line_item: A product or service line added to a record, such as a deal, with its name, quantity and price. (type, id, name, quantity, unit_price; optional notes). send_record: An invoice or quote emailed to the customer by the person's own system, from its own email address. The customer receives it, and only the person can approve it. (type, id; optional email). convert_estimate: A new invoice with the lines of a quote, linked to it and not sent; nothing is made when the quote already has one. (type, id). convert_lead: A lead made into a new estimate or a new job, or into a contact, in the person's system, which then counts as converted; it cannot be turned back, and only the person can approve it. (type, id, into). link_records: Two records linked in the person's system, such as a contact to a deal, or an existing note or task to another record; nothing changes when they are linked already. (type, id, other_type, other_id; optional other_parent). unlink_records: The link between two records removed; both records stay as they are, and only the person can approve it. (type, id, other_type, other_id; optional other_parent). create_item: A new item next to the six record types, such as a product, a coupon, a custom record, a project task or a custom field, with the values its kind takes. A system looks for the same item first and makes none when it exists. (item_kind, values; optional parent). update_item: New values for an item next to the six record types, such as a product price, a coupon, a custom record or a pipeline's stages; only what is given changes. (item_kind, item_id, values; optional parent). set_item_state: An item switched on or off, published or set back to draft, or a schedule started or cancelled, such as a workflow, a calendar group or an invoice schedule. (item_kind, item_id, state; optional parent). move_item: An item moved to another list, group or place, such as a project task to another list. (item_kind, item_id, to; optional parent). add_tag: Tags put on a record, such as a contact; a tag can start an automation in the person's system. (type, id, tags). remove_tag: Tags taken off a record; tags it does not carry are left alone. (type, id, tags). add_follower: Users who follow a record and hear of what happens on it. (type, id, users). remove_follower: Users who no longer follow a record. (type, id, users). add_to_workflow: A record put into one of the person's own workflows or campaigns, which then runs its steps, and may send messages. Only the person can approve it. (type, id, workflow; optional automation_kind, start_at). remove_from_workflow: A record taken out of a workflow or campaign, so its next steps do not run for it. Only the person can approve it. (type, id, workflow; optional automation_kind). update_note: The text of a note that already exists, by the id list_related_records gives it. (type, id, note_id, text). send_message: An email or text message sent to a contact from the person's own system, as part of the conversation with them. The contact receives it, and only the person can approve it. (type, id, channel, text; optional subject, email, send_at). update_conversation: A conversation marked read or unread, or starred, by the id list_related_records gives it. (conversation_id; optional read, starred). record_payment: A payment the customer made elsewhere, such as in cash or by bank transfer, written on an invoice or order; no card is charged. Only the person can approve it, and it is never undone from here. (id, amount, method; optional type, item_kind, paid_at, reference, notes). change_consent: A contact subscribed to or unsubscribed from the email the person's system sends. Only the person can approve it. (type, id, subscribed; optional reason). void_record: An invoice or quote voided in the person's system, so nothing is owed on it any more; it stays there, marked void. Only the person can approve it, and it is never undone from here. (type, id). send_document: A document or contract sent for signing from the person's own system, either one that exists or a new one made from a template for a contact. The recipients receive it, and only the person can approve it. (item_kind, item_id, user; optional type, id). Nothing is written yet: the answer shows, per record, what it holds now and would hold after, plus a proposal id. Show it to the person, say so first when something would be sent to the people in their system, ask whether to go ahead, and only then call apply_proposal; when needsApproval is true, share the approve link instead. Not for reading (use search_records or get_record). Never deletes; a payment waits for the person's approval.

action.description: What to propose; set_fields when left out.

items.description: One object per record, at most 25, with the values the action takes.

amount.description: record_payment: How much was paid, as a number.

at.description: add_note: When the note is from, ISO 8601 in UTC; now when left out. log_activity: When it took place, ISO 8601 in UTC; now when left out.

automation_kind.description: add_to_workflow, remove_from_workflow: A workflow or a campaign; workflow when left out.

clear.description: set_fields: field keys to empty; only fields describe_record_type marks clearable.

conversation_id.description: update_conversation: The id of the conversation, as list_related_records gives it.

done.description: add_task: True for a task that is already done. update_task: True when the task is done, false to open it again.

due_at.description: add_task: When it is due, ISO 8601 in UTC. update_task: When it is due now, ISO 8601 in UTC.

email.description: send_record: Send to this address instead of the one on the record. send_message: Send to this address of the contact instead of their main one.

end_at.description: log_activity: When a meeting ended, ISO 8601 in UTC.

fields.description: update_fields: Field names and their new values as text; an empty text empties a field.

id.description: The id of the record in the system. Leave it out with set_fields to make a new record, and with update_task where the system does not ask for it.

item_id.description: update_item, set_item_state, move_item: The id of the item, as list_items gives it. send_document: The id of the document or template, as list_items gives it.

item_kind.description: create_item: Which kind of item to make. update_item: Which kind of item to change. set_item_state, move_item: Which kind of item it is. record_payment: For an order, the kind order instead of a type. send_document: A document that exists, or a template to make one from.

name.description: add_line_item: The name of the line.

note_id.description: update_note: The id of the note, as list_related_records gives it.

notes.description: add_task: More text on the task. update_task: The new text on the task. log_activity: More text on it. add_line_item: More text on the line. record_payment: More text on the payment.

other_id.description: link_records, unlink_records: The id of the second record in the system.

other_parent.description: link_records, unlink_records: For a custom record, the object it belongs to, as list_items gives it.

other_type.description: link_records, unlink_records: The type of the second record: a record type, a business or a custom record.

paid_at.description: record_payment: When it was paid, ISO 8601; today when left out.

parent.description: create_item, update_item, set_item_state, move_item: The item it sits in, where the kind needs one: the object of a custom record, the product of a price, the project of a task, the task of a comment.

pipeline.description: move_stage: The id of the pipeline, only when the stage is in another pipeline than the record's.

quantity.description: add_line_item: How many, as a number.

read.description: update_conversation: True to mark it read, false to mark it unread.

reason.description: change_consent: Why, as the person said it.

reference.description: record_payment: A reference, such as a cheque or bank transfer number.

send_at.description: send_message: When to send it, ISO 8601 in UTC; now when left out.

set.description: set_fields: field keys as describe_record_type names them (email, phone, address.city) and their new values. A money field takes a number.

stage.description: move_stage: The id of the stage to move to, as describe_record_type gives it with include stages.

starred.description: update_conversation: True to star it, false to take the star off.

start_at.description: add_to_workflow: When it starts, ISO 8601 in UTC; now when left out.

state.description: set_item_state: The state to put it in.

subject.description: add_task: The title of the task. update_task: The new title of the task. send_message: The subject of an email.

subscribed.description: change_consent: True to subscribe the contact, false to unsubscribe them.

tags.description: add_tag: The tags to add, at most 20. remove_tag: The tags to remove, at most 20.

task_id.description: update_task: The id of the task, as list_related_records or search_tasks gives it.

task_kind.description: add_task: What kind of task it is.

text.description: add_note: The text of the note. update_note: The new text of the note. send_message: The text of the message.

to.description: move_item: The id of the list, group or place to move it to.

type.description: The record type; link_records and unlink_records also take note or task as the first record. update_task only needs it where the system asks for it.

unit_price.description: add_line_item: The price of one, as a number.

user.description: add_note: The id of the user shown as its writer, as describe_record_type gives it with include users. add_task: The id of the user the task is for, as describe_record_type gives it with include users. update_task: The id of the user the task is for now, as describe_record_type gives it with include users. log_activity: The id of the user who had it, as describe_record_type gives it with include users; some systems need it for a meeting. send_document: The id of the user it is sent from, as describe_record_type gives it with include users.

users.description: add_follower, remove_follower: The ids of the users, as describe_record_type gives them with include users.

values.description: create_item: The values of the new item, as get_item shows them for an item of this kind. update_item: The values to change, as get_item shows them.

workflow.description: add_to_workflow, remove_from_workflow: The id of the workflow or campaign, as list_items gives it.

system.description: Which AI agent: the system's id from get_ai_agents_info, or the name of the system or its connection. Ask the person which AI agent they mean unless they named it in this conversation; never pick one yourself.

name: propose_changes
title: Propose changes to records
